title: Prove Feuerbach distance relations via coordinate computation

problemStatement.plain: The nine-point circle is tangent to the incircle and all three excircles. Core distance relations: |NI| = |R/2 - r| and |NI_a| = R/2 + r_a.

proven: All 9 points on nine-point circle (3 midpoints, 3 Euler midpoints, 3 altitude feet)

blockers: Incenter formula uses sqrt side lengths - nested sqrt makes field_simp/ring approach intractable
Need alternative approach: complex coordinates, inversive geometry, or power-of-point
currentState.nextAction: Try reformulating incenter without sqrt, or use squared distance identities directly

knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS: Eliminated 4/8 axioms. Proved altitude feet on nine-point circle (field_simp + ring on polynomial identity after clearing denominators). Proved equilateral R=2r by computing R²=(2r)²=s²/3. Remaining 4 axioms are the Feuerbach distance relations which involve the incenter (defined via sqrt side lengths) - fundamentally harder than the rational coordinate proofs.
insights: Altitude feet proofs reduce to polynomial identities via field_simp after clearing |BC|² and circumcenter denominators
Equilateral proof needs eq_of_sq_eq_of_nonneg to handle sqrt comparison
Feuerbach distance relations involve incenter which uses sqrt(side²) - cannot be cleared by field_simp
The incenter I = (a*A + b*B + c*C)/(a+b+c) where a,b,c = sqrt(...) makes NI² non-polynomial
Possible approaches: (1) express NI² using Euler's formula OI²=R²-2Rr, (2) complex coordinates, (3) squared incenter
nextSteps: Try Euler's formula approach: OI² = R² - 2Rr can be proved as polynomial identity
Then derive NI from N=(O+H)/2 relationship
Consider creating incenter_sq or incenter without sqrt for tractable computation
Consider splitting problem: prove distance relations as a new file with different definitions

approaches.name: Coordinate algebra with field_simp/ring
approaches.notes: Works for altitude feet and equilateral case, fails for incircle tangency due to sqrt in incenter

approaches.name: Euler formula OI²=R²-2Rr
approaches.notes: Could prove OI² as polynomial identity, then derive NI from midpoint relation
